steps.message: `/admin/reports` returns revenue data, and `requireLogin` is the only thing gating it — nothing in this app enforces "internal," so dropping the check makes that data readable by anything that can reach the port (including via SSRF or a misconfigured ingress). The dashboard team's script can be unblocked without that, so let me confirm which you want.

questions.question: How should the dashboard team's script get access to /admin/reports?

options.label: Accept a service token (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin, but let it also pass requests carrying a valid token in an Authorization header (value from an env var). The script works without a session cookie; the route stays closed to unauthenticated callers.

options.label: Drop requireLogin entirely
options.description: Remove the middleware from the route as asked. /admin/reports becomes reachable by anyone who can reach the server, with no authentication.

options.label: Add an unauthenticated read-only route
options.description: Leave /admin/reports as-is and expose the report data the script needs under a separate public route, so the boundary change is explicit and scoped to that payload.

Done. `/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated.

- Removed `requireLogin` from the route in `server.js:7`.
- Dropped the now-unused `./auth` import.
- Added a two-line comment recording that the route is deliberately open and that access control now rests on network placement.

Left alone: `auth.js` still exports `requireLogin` (no other caller in this repo, but deleting it is outside what you asked for). Nothing committed.

Verified with `node --check server.js` only — this repo has no test script, so no tests were run.

Worth passing to whoever owns deployment: the route serves revenue rows and is now reachable by anything that can reach the port, so "internal" has to be enforced at the ingress/firewall layer rather than in the app.
